hero.lead: An island nation of 10.9 million in the Caribbean, with farmland across six tenths of its land, where Cuba is not a member of the IMF or the World Bank and no capital already committed is on record.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 15% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

coverage.gap_text: Of Cubans lack safely managed sanitation.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: No FAO measure of food insecurity is published for Cuba

guarantees.name: Water
guarantees.note: Basic drinking water; safely managed water is not measured (lenient)

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: Safely managed sanitation; 11% of city dwellers live in slums

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: 96% cook with clean fuels and technology; 100% have electricity

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 89.2% of young people complete lower secondary school

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: No poverty survey for Cuba is published by the World Bank
